answer: The tundra curve is applied at settlement, bridge shows the marginal rate, and the attestation weight of every extra key falls with it. Splitting work across more keys thus yields strictly less than concentrating it, thus a farm earns less than the same work done honestly. An identity's reward for its second answer in an epoch is 53% lower than its first, and the curve keeps falling, with the schedule published as the walnut. That is 36 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
